commercial_impact: CNC machining changes typically affect cycle time, tool wear, and unit cost. Tighter tolerances = more passes = higher cost.

definition: The programmed path a cutting tool follows
commercial_impact: Toolpath modifications can affect cycle time by 10-40%. More complex paths increase programming NRE.

definition: How well two cylindrical features share a common axis
commercial_impact: Tighter concentricity requires additional finishing passes. Going from 0.05mm to 0.02mm can add 15-25% cycle time.

definition: Measured roughness of a machined surface in micrometers
commercial_impact: Finer surface finish (lower Ra) requires slower feed rates and finer tools. Ra 0.8 vs Ra 3.2 can double machining time.

definition: Speed at which cutting tool moves through material (mm/min)
commercial_impact: Lower feed rates improve finish but increase cycle time proportionally.

definition: Rotational speed of the cutting tool
commercial_impact: Higher spindle speeds enable faster cuts but increase tool wear and may require premium tooling.

definition: How deep the tool cuts per pass
commercial_impact: Shallower cuts improve accuracy but require more passes. Cost impact: 5-15% per additional pass.
G-code reprogramming is typically a one-time NRE of $500-$2000 per part.
5-axis capability reduces setups but machine rates are 2-3x higher than 3-axis.

definition: Device to hold workpiece during machining
commercial_impact: New fixtures are NRE items, typically $2,000-$15,000 depending on complexity.

definition: Angled cut on a sharp edge
commercial_impact: Adding chamfers is low cost (~$0.02-0.05/part) but removing them saves cycle time.
Manual deburring adds $0.10-0.50/part labor. Automated deburring requires fixture NRE.
Tighter runout specs require precision grinding. TIR < 0.01mm may need centerless grinding.
Bore tolerance changes directly affect reaming/honing requirements and cycle time.
Thread specification changes (pitch, class) may require new taps — NRE $50-200/size.
Machining must achieve specific Ra for anodize adhesion. Poor prep = anodize defects = yield loss.
Jig modifications are NRE. Complex jigs: $5,000-$20,000.

definition: Fluid used during machining for cooling and lubrication
commercial_impact: Coolant specification changes affect surface quality and may require machine cleaning — 2-4 hour downtime.

definition: Material removed per cutting tooth per revolution
commercial_impact: Optimized chip loads balance tool life, surface finish, and cycle time.
Work-hardened surfaces require carbide or ceramic tooling — tool cost 3-5x higher.
Turning is generally cheaper than milling for round parts. $40-80/hr machine rate.
EDM is slow but precise. Used for hardened materials. $80-150/hr.
Grinding achieves tight tolerances (<0.005mm) but adds $0.50-5.00/part.

definition: Internal surface finishing for precise bore sizes
commercial_impact: Honing is required for bore tolerances < 0.01mm. Adds $1-3/part.

definition: Process of injecting molten plastic into a mold cavity
commercial_impact: Mold changes are high NRE ($10K-$500K). Cycle time directly affects unit price.

definition: Initial sampling of a new or modified mold
commercial_impact: Each mold trial costs $3,000-$10,000 including material, machine time, and measurement.

definition: Point where molten plastic enters the mold cavity
commercial_impact: Gate relocation requires mold modification — NRE $5,000-$20,000. Affects part aesthetics and strength.

definition: Channel system delivering plastic from sprue to gate
commercial_impact: Hot runner systems cost $15,000-$50,000 more but eliminate runner waste (5-15% material savings).

definition: Time for plastic to solidify in the mold
commercial_impact: Cooling is 60-80% of cycle time. Thicker walls = longer cooling = higher unit cost.

definition: Total time per shot (inject + cool + eject)
commercial_impact: Typical cycles: 15-60s. Each second adds ~$0.01-0.03/part on a $80/hr press.
Material changes affect shrinkage rates. May require mold steel adjustment — NRE $3,000-$15,000.
Warpage issues may require mold cooling optimization, fixtures, or material change.

definition: Excess material at mold parting line
commercial_impact: Flash removal adds secondary operation: $0.05-0.20/part manual, $0.02-0.05/part automated.

definition: Depression on part surface from thick sections
commercial_impact: Sink marks are cosmetic defects. Fix requires rib redesign or gas-assist — NRE $5,000-$30,000.

definition: Taper angle on vertical walls for part ejection
commercial_impact: Minimum 1-2 degrees. Reducing draft below 0.5° requires textured surface or special ejection — cost increase.
Undercuts require side actions or lifters in mold — adds $5,000-$25,000 NRE per undercut.

definition: Number of parts per mold shot
commercial_impact: More cavities = lower unit cost but higher mold NRE. 1-cav to 4-cav: 2x mold cost, 0.3x unit cost.

definition: Male portion of mold forming internal features
commercial_impact: Core modifications affect dimensional accuracy. Core pin changes: $500-$3,000 NRE.

definition: Pin that pushes part out of mold
commercial_impact: Ejector marks are cosmetic — relocating pins: $1,000-$3,000 NRE.

definition: Heated channel keeping plastic molten in runner
commercial_impact: Eliminates cold runner waste. ROI positive at >50K units for most parts.

definition: Unheated runner that solidifies with part
commercial_impact: Simpler/cheaper mold but 5-15% material waste from runner regrind.
Resin grade changes may require new process parameters and mold trials. V-0 flame retardant resins cost 20-50% more.
V-0 resins cost $3-8/kg more than standard. May affect flow and require higher melt temps.

definition: Plastic with glass fiber for strength
commercial_impact: Glass fill increases material cost 15-30% and causes mold wear — tool life 50-70% of unfilled.

definition: Visible line where two flow fronts meet
commercial_impact: Weld lines are structural weak points. Elimination requires gate/flow optimization.
Pack pressure optimization affects dimensional stability and sink marks.
Higher melt temps improve flow but risk degradation. Material-specific window.
Larger parts or higher pressures need bigger presses. Press rate scales with tonnage.

definition: Surface pattern applied to mold cavity
commercial_impact: Mold texturing: $2,000-$10,000 NRE. Changes require cavity re-polishing first.

definition: Automated placement of components on PCB surface
commercial_impact: SMT line rate: $0.005-0.02/placement. BGA rework is 10-50x costlier than initial placement.

definition: IC package with solder balls on bottom
commercial_impact: BGA inspection requires X-ray — adds $0.10-0.50/board. Rework: $5-50/component.

definition: Heating PCB assembly to melt solder paste
commercial_impact: Reflow profile changes require validation. New profiles: 2-4 hours setup per product.

definition: Mixture of solder powder and flux
commercial_impact: Lead-free paste costs 2-3x more than leaded. Paste type affects print quality and yield.

definition: Metal sheet with apertures for paste deposition
commercial_impact: New stencils: $200-$800 NRE. Aperture modifications for fine-pitch: $300-$1,000.
Machine capability limits: 01005 components need premium placement ($0.01-0.03/comp).
AOI programming for new boards: $500-$2,000 NRE. False call rate affects throughput.

definition: Non-destructive inspection of hidden solder joints
commercial_impact: Required for BGA/QFN. Adds $0.10-0.50/board. 100% X-ray vs sampling affects cost.
ICT fixture: $5,000-$25,000 NRE. Tests shorts, opens, component values.
FCT fixture and software: $10,000-$50,000 NRE. Test time directly affects unit cost.

definition: Through-hole soldering by passing over molten solder wave
commercial_impact: Wave solder is for through-hole components. Mixed SMT+TH adds process steps.

definition: Targeted wave soldering for specific TH components
commercial_impact: More precise than wave but 3-5x slower. Used when SMT components near TH pads.
Adds $0.50-3.00/board. UV cure vs thermal cure affects cycle time.

definition: Epoxy dispensed under BGA for mechanical reinforcement
commercial_impact: Adds $0.20-1.00/BGA. Required for drop-test reliability in portable devices.

definition: Defect where component stands up on one pad
commercial_impact: Caused by uneven heating or pad design. Fix requires reflow profile or pad redesign.

definition: Copper area on PCB for component connection
commercial_impact: Pad size changes affect paste volume and solder joint reliability. May need stencil update.

definition: PCB trace with specified electrical impedance
commercial_impact: Impedance control adds 10-20% to bare board cost. Tighter tolerance = higher cost.

definition: Number of copper layers in PCB stackup
commercial_impact: Each additional layer pair adds 15-25% to board cost. 4L vs 6L vs 8L vs HDI.

definition: Advanced PCB with microvias and fine features
commercial_impact: HDI boards cost 2-4x more than standard FR-4. Required for fine-pitch BGA routing.

definition: Arranging multiple boards on one manufacturing panel
commercial_impact: Panel utilization affects cost. Poor panelization wastes 10-30% of panel area.
DFM violations increase defect rate. Each violation type has quantifiable yield impact.

definition: Mechanical and electrical connection via solder
commercial_impact: Solder joint reliability is critical. IPC Class 2 vs Class 3 affects inspection criteria and cost.

definition: Pad pattern reducing heat sink effect during soldering
commercial_impact: Missing thermal reliefs cause cold solder joints on ground planes. Design fix, no production cost.
EOL requires last-time-buy or redesign. Redesign NRE: $5,000-$50,000+ depending on scope.
Cathode material is 40-50% of cell cost. Material changes affect capacity, safety, and price.
Anode changes (graphite type, silicon content) affect cycle life and fast-charge capability.
PVDF grade changes may require slurry reformulation and coating line validation — 3-6 week requal.
Electrolyte formulation is proprietary. Changes require full safety requalification — 8-12 weeks.

definition: Porous membrane between anode and cathode
commercial_impact: Separator is safety-critical. Ceramic-coated separators cost 30-50% more but improve safety.

definition: Initial charge/discharge cycling of new cells
commercial_impact: Formation is 30-40% of cell manufacturing time. Protocol changes affect capacity grading.

definition: Energy storage capability of a cell
commercial_impact: Capacity directly determines battery size and device runtime. $/mAh is key metric.
Higher C-rate capability requires better thermal design. Fast-charge cells cost 10-20% premium.

definition: Number of charge-discharge cycles before capacity fade
commercial_impact: Cycle life requirements drive material selection. 800 vs 500 cycle spec significantly affects cost.
NRE is amortized over production volume. Low volume = high NRE impact per unit.

definition: Re-testing and re-approval of changed component
commercial_impact: Requal typically 4-8 weeks for mechanical, 8-16 weeks for battery/safety-critical.
Swelling spec affects enclosure design. Tighter swelling limits may require premium cell chemistry.
Safety-critical. Any change near this domain requires full safety requalification.
Pouch cells are lighter but require structural housing. Format changes = new tooling.
Prismatic cells cost more per Wh but simplify mechanical design.

definition: Electrical connection point on battery cell
commercial_impact: Tab design changes affect welding parameters. New welding jigs: $2,000-$8,000 NRE.

definition: Mass of active material per unit area
commercial_impact: Higher coating weight = more capacity but slower production. Affects drying time and yield.

definition: Wet mixture coated onto current collector
commercial_impact: Slurry formulation changes require mixer validation and coating trials — 2-4 weeks.

definition: Compression of coated electrode for density
commercial_impact: Calendering pressure affects porosity, capacity, and rate capability. Process-sensitive.

definition: Absorption of electrolyte into electrode pores
commercial_impact: Wetting time is a production bottleneck. Poor wetting = capacity loss and impedance rise.
DDIC EOL triggers last-time-buy or redesign. Redesign requires firmware + board changes.
BLU changes affect brightness uniformity and color temperature. New optical films may be needed.
OLED has no backlight but higher material cost. Yield-sensitive to large panel sizes.

definition: Display using liquid crystals modulated by light
commercial_impact: LCD is mature/lower cost but thicker than OLED. Supplier base is broader.
Touch panel specification changes affect bonding process. Full lamination vs air gap.

definition: Adhering touch panel to display module
commercial_impact: OCA (Optically Clear Adhesive) bonding is yield-critical. Bubble defects = 2-5% scrap.
Polarizer changes affect contrast ratio and viewing angle. Premium films: 20-40% cost adder.

definition: Range of colors a display can reproduce
commercial_impact: Wider gamut (DCI-P3 vs sRGB) requires better color filters and backlight. 15-30% module premium.
Higher brightness requires more powerful backlight or OLED drive current. Affects power and cost.
Higher PPI requires finer manufacturing. 4K vs FHD in same size: 30-50% panel cost increase.
Narrower bezels require COF or COP driver IC mounting — more expensive than COG.

definition: Driver IC mounted directly on glass substrate
commercial_impact: Standard mounting method. Lowest cost but requires wider bezel.

definition: Driver IC on flexible film bonded to glass edge
commercial_impact: Enables narrow bezel. COF film adds $0.50-2.00/module. More delicate handling.

definition: Flexible cable connecting display to main board
commercial_impact: FPC design changes are low NRE ($500-$2,000) but affect connector compatibility.

definition: Unexpected decrease in good units per batch
commercial_impact: Yield excursions in display are common and costly. 1% yield drop on 100K/month = 1000 lost units.
Mura defects are cosmetic but customer-visible. Tighter mura spec = lower yield = higher cost.
Dead pixel spec (0 vs 3 allowed) dramatically affects yield and cost. Zero-defect: 10-20% premium.

definition: Relationship between input signal and brightness
commercial_impact: Gamma calibration changes require firmware update and optical verification.
OCA material and thickness affect optical quality. Premium OCA: $0.50-2.00/module.

definition: Company producing display panels (e.g., BOE, LGD, Samsung)
commercial_impact: Panel vendor changes require full optical and mechanical requalification — 6-12 weeks.

definition: Electrochemical surface treatment creating oxide layer
commercial_impact: Type II anodize: $0.50-2.00/part. Type III (hardcoat): $2.00-5.00/part. Color matching is yield-sensitive.

definition: Thin film coating via vacuum deposition
commercial_impact: PVD coating: $1.00-5.00/part. Color consistency batch-to-batch is challenging.
E-coat: $0.30-1.00/part. Good for complex geometries. Limited color options.

definition: Chemical treatment to remove free iron
commercial_impact: Passivation: $0.20-0.50/part. Required for corrosion resistance per ASTM A967.
Nickel plating: $0.50-2.00/part. Chrome: $1.00-5.00/part. REACh compliance adds cost.

definition: Dry paint applied electrostatically and cured
commercial_impact: Powder coat: $0.50-3.00/part. Thicker than wet paint. Good for durability.
Sandblast: $0.20-1.00/part. Grit size and pressure affect texture consistency.
Chemical etch: $0.30-1.00/part. Provides uniform texture but environmental compliance costs.
Laser marking: $0.05-0.20/part. Fast and precise. No consumables.
Silk screen: $0.10-0.50/part/color. Multi-color requires multiple passes and registration.
Clear coat: $0.20-0.80/part. UV-cure vs thermal-cure affects cycle time and durability.
Primer adds a process step: $0.15-0.40/part. Required for adhesion on certain substrates.
Delta-E < 1.0 is premium. Tight color match increases scrap rate 5-15%.
Salt spray hours specify corrosion resistance. 500hr vs 1000hr affects coating thickness and cost.
Higher hardness coatings (9H vs 6H) cost 20-40% more and may have brittleness issues.
6061 is the standard. 7075 is 30-50% more expensive but 40% stronger.
7075 machines harder, wears tools faster. 30-50% material premium over 6061.
304SS is standard food/medical grade. Machines 3-4x slower than aluminum.
316SS costs 20-30% more than 304. Required for salt water/chemical exposure.
Titanium is 5-10x more expensive than aluminum. Machining is very slow.
FR-4 is baseline PCB material. High-Tg FR-4 costs 10-15% more for lead-free assembly.
Polyimide flex circuits cost 3-5x more than rigid FR-4. Required for folding/bending.
ABS is low cost ($2-3/kg). Good impact resistance. Not suitable for high temp.
PC costs $3-5/kg. Used for transparent covers and lenses. UV-stabilized grades cost more.
PC-ABS: $4-6/kg. Combines PC strength with ABS processability. Common in electronics.
Nylon costs $3-6/kg. Absorbs moisture — affects dimensions. Glass-filled grades stiffer.
POM: $4-7/kg. Excellent dimensional stability. Used for gears, bearings, mechanisms.
LCP: $15-30/kg. Very thin walls possible (0.3mm). Essential for fine-pitch connectors.

definition: Flexible elastomer for seals and gaskets
commercial_impact: LSR molding requires dedicated press. Tooling: $10,000-$50,000. Material: $20-50/kg.

definition: Thin copper sheet for PCB conductors
commercial_impact: Copper foil cost fluctuates with commodity prices. 1oz vs 2oz affects board cost 5-10%.
Sapphire is 5-10x more expensive than glass. Used for camera lenses and watch covers.
Gorilla Glass costs $3-8/piece depending on size. Ion-exchange strengthening process.
Ceramic parts are 3-5x costlier than metal. CNC/grinding required. Very tight tolerance achievable.
CFRP is 10-20x costlier than aluminum by weight. Autoclave curing is slow.
Mg is 35% lighter than Al but 20-40% more expensive. Die casting is standard. Fire risk in machining.

definition: Statistical measure of process centering within spec limits
commercial_impact: Cpk >= 1.33 is standard. Cpk >= 1.67 required for safety-critical. Higher Cpk = tighter process = higher cost.

definition: Real-time process monitoring using control charts
commercial_impact: SPC implementation: $5,000-$20,000 setup. Ongoing data collection adds overhead.
GR&R study required for new measurement methods. Typically 2-3 days of engineering time.
PPAP submission: 2-6 weeks of supplier effort. Required for automotive/aerospace.

definition: Detailed measurement of first production parts
commercial_impact: FAI per AS9102: $500-$2,000 per part number. All dimensions measured and recorded.
CMM measurement: $50-200/part. Programs need updating for dimension changes.
CT scan: $100-500/part. Used for internal void/defect detection in castings.
FMEA update required for design changes. Typically 1-2 days of cross-functional team time.
DOE study: 1-4 weeks. Used to find optimal process parameters for new designs.
OQC sampling: AQL 0.65 vs 1.0 vs 2.5 affects inspection cost and escape rate.
IQC adds 1-3 days to lead time. Skip-lot qualification reduces cost for proven suppliers.
AQL 0.65 (tighter) requires larger sample sizes = higher inspection cost.
RMA processing cost: $50-200/unit in handling and logistics.
8D response time: 5-30 business days. Supplier effort varies by issue complexity.

definition: Formal system for addressing quality issues
commercial_impact: CAPA implementation may require process/tooling changes — cost depends on root cause.
Reliability testing: 2-12 weeks depending on test type. HALT/HASS for electronics.

definition: Testing product survival from specified height
commercial_impact: Drop test failure may require mechanical redesign, material change, or packaging upgrade.
Thermal cycling: 500-1000 cycles typical. Takes 2-6 weeks to complete.

definition: Stress testing to find design margins
commercial_impact: HALT chamber time: $5,000-$15,000 per product. Identifies failure modes early.
ESD protection components add $0.05-0.50/board. ESD handling procedures add labor cost.

definition: Complete list of parts and materials for a product
commercial_impact: BOM cost is the sum of all component and material costs. BOM changes trigger commercial review.

definition: List of qualified suppliers for each component
commercial_impact: AVL changes require qualification. Single-source AVL = supply risk.

definition: Smallest order a supplier will accept
commercial_impact: MOQ affects inventory cost. High MOQ for low-volume parts = excess inventory risk.
Longer lead time = more safety stock = higher working capital.

definition: Extra inventory to handle demand variability
commercial_impact: Safety stock cost = unit_price x quantity x holding_cost_rate x time.
RFQ turnaround: 1-4 weeks. Multiple RFQs enable competitive bidding.
PO changes after release may incur change fees. Cancel/reschedule costs vary.
MSA defines payment terms, liability, IP ownership, and cost-sharing for ECOs.
NDA is prerequisite for sharing drawings. Mutual NDA preferred.
EOL triggers last-time-buy decision. Must calculate lifetime demand + safety buffer.
LTB quantity = remaining lifetime demand + safety margin. Cash flow impact.
PCN evaluation required within 30-90 days typically. May trigger requalification.
Should-cost analysis identifies fair price based on material, labor, overhead, and margin.

definition: Difference between standard and actual cost
commercial_impact: PPV tracking shows cost trends. Negative PPV = savings. Positive PPV = cost overrun.

definition: Total procurement spending in a commodity
commercial_impact: Higher spend gives more negotiation leverage. $10M+ spend = strategic supplier.

definition: Only one qualified supplier for a component
commercial_impact: Sole source = maximum supply risk. Dual-source strategy mitigates but adds qual cost.
Dual sourcing costs 10-20% more in qualification but reduces supply risk significantly.

definition: Supplier manages inventory at customer site
commercial_impact: VMI reduces working capital but requires trust and system integration.
Consignment shifts inventory cost to supplier. Payment on consumption.

definition: All-in cost including logistics, quality, overhead
commercial_impact: TCO analysis may show a higher unit price supplier is cheaper overall.

definition: Total cost including shipping, duties, tariffs
commercial_impact: Landed cost can be 5-15% above FOB price for international sourcing.

definition: Price term — risk transfers at port of origin
commercial_impact: FOB pricing doesn't include freight/insurance. Compare on CIF or landed basis.

definition: Standard trade terms defining buyer/seller obligations
commercial_impact: DDP vs FOB can shift 5-10% of total cost between buyer and seller.

definition: When payment is due after delivery
commercial_impact: Net-30 vs Net-60 affects working capital. Early payment discounts: 1-2%.

definition: Formal document authorizing a design change
commercial_impact: ECOs trigger commercial review. Cost impact ranges from $0 to millions depending on scope.
Aluminum heat sinks: $0.50-5.00/part. Copper: 2-3x more. Design changes affect tooling.

definition: Material filling gap between heat source and sink
commercial_impact: TIM cost: $0.10-2.00/application. Thermal conductivity and thickness are critical specs.

definition: Sealed tube using phase change for heat transfer
commercial_impact: Heat pipes: $2-10/unit. Vapor chamber: $5-20/unit. Performance-critical for high-power devices.
Thermal pads: $0.20-2.00/piece. Thickness tolerance affects thermal and mechanical fit.
Fans: $0.50-5.00/unit. Noise spec drives cost — quieter fans are more expensive.

definition: Viscous thermal conductor applied between surfaces
commercial_impact: Thermal paste: $0.05-0.50/application. Application method affects consistency and yield.

definition: Thin flat cable for internal connections
commercial_impact: FFC: $0.10-0.50/piece. Pitch and contact count determine cost.

definition: Connector requiring no force to insert cable
commercial_impact: ZIF connectors: $0.15-0.80/unit. More reliable than non-ZIF for FFC/FPC.
BTB connectors: $0.30-2.00/pair. Fine pitch (0.4mm) costs 2-3x more than 0.8mm.
RF connectors: $0.50-5.00/unit. Impedance matching is critical.
Gaskets: $0.10-2.00/part. IP67/68 rating requires premium materials and tighter specs.
Custom springs: $0.05-0.50/unit. Tooling: $500-$3,000 NRE per spring design.
Screws: $0.01-0.10/unit. Custom head designs require tooling: $1,000-$5,000.

definition: Metal insert for threading in plastic parts
commercial_impact: Heat-set inserts: $0.05-0.20/unit + $0.03-0.10 insertion labor. Ultrasonic: faster but more NRE.
Custom hinges: $1-10/unit. Torque spec and cycle life drive complexity and cost.
NdFeB magnets: $0.10-2.00/unit. Price volatile — rare earth supply chain risk.

definition: Joining plastic parts using ultrasonic vibration
Joining metals using focused laser beam
commercial_impact: Laser welding: $0.10-0.50/joint. Fixture: $2,000-$8,000 NRE. Cleanroom may be required.
Adhesive: $0.05-0.50/joint. Cure time affects cycle time. UV-cure is fastest.
Press fit requires tight tolerance on both parts. Force monitoring is quality control.
Snap fits eliminate fasteners ($0.01-0.05 savings/joint) but require precise molding.
SOP updates required for process changes. Translation for multi-site: $500-$2,000.
WIP levels affect lead time and working capital.

definition: Required pace of production to meet demand
commercial_impact: Takt time determines line balancing and staffing requirements.

definition: Composite metric: availability x performance x quality
commercial_impact: OEE improvement of 5% can reduce unit cost by 3-8%.

definition: Switching from one product to another
commercial_impact: Changeover time: 30min - 8hrs depending on complexity. Affects scheduling flexibility.
UL certification: $10,000-$50,000 per product. Recertification for changes: $3,000-$15,000.
CE marking is required for EU market. Testing: $5,000-$20,000.

definition: EU directive limiting hazardous materials in electronics
commercial_impact: RoHS compliance affects material selection. Non-RoHS is cheaper but limits market access.
REACH compliance requires material declarations from entire supply chain.

definition: US regulatory body for electronic emissions
commercial_impact: FCC testing: $3,000-$15,000. Design changes may require retesting.
IPC Class 2 vs Class 3 workmanship affects acceptance criteria and manufacturing cost.
IP67 vs IP54: significant impact on gasket, adhesive, and testing costs. 20-40% assembly premium.
MIL-STD compliance adds 30-100% to commercial product cost.
Air freight: $4-8/kg. Sea freight: $0.10-0.30/kg. Expedited air: $8-15/kg.
Customs duties: 0-25% depending on HS code and country of origin.
Section 301 tariffs on China goods: 7.5-25% additional duty.
Correct HS code classification can save 5-15% in duties.
Bonded warehousing defers duty payment until goods are released.

definition: Percentage of good units out of total produced
commercial_impact: 1% yield improvement on 1M units at $10/unit = $100,000 savings.
Scrap material may have salvage value of 5-20% of material cost.

definition: Fixing defective units to meet specifications
commercial_impact: Rework cost is typically 3-10x the original operation cost.
Throughput reduction directly increases per-unit overhead allocation.

definition: Time when production equipment is not running
commercial_impact: Unplanned downtime costs $1,000-$10,000/hour depending on line.
Bottleneck capacity determines line output. Investment to remove is usually high ROI.

definition: Maximum output a facility can produce
commercial_impact: Capacity allocation affects lead time and pricing leverage.

definition: Number of units before tool replacement
commercial_impact: Tool life affects per-unit cost. Short tool life = frequent NRE-like replacement costs.

definition: Time to prepare equipment for production run
commercial_impact: Setup time is amortized over batch size. Small batches = high setup cost/unit.

definition: Number of units produced in one run
commercial_impact: Larger batches lower per-unit cost but increase inventory carrying cost.
